title: Expected Mac Running a Build Outside Approved Update Policy
exclusions: Compares the newest MDM-reported `OSVersion` and `BuildVersion` for expected Macs with an exact, deployment-owned approved-build policy keyed by cohort and build. It reports missing 48-hour inventory, status older than 24 hours, missing version/build, or a build not currently approved. Exact build matching avoids incorrect lexicographic version comparison. This UC does not prove an update is available/applicable, inspect pending-update state, cover apps or Background Security Improvements, enforce a deadline, assess vulnerabilities, or satisfy any regulation. The previous duplicate ASD/APRA mappings and seven-year evidence claim were removed as unsupported.
evidence: Retain `expected_macos_approved_build_posture`, its schedule/results/alerts; signed expected-device, approved-build, and exception lookup revisions with source URL, decision, effective/expiry dates and approver; redacted MDM DeviceInformation responses and collection health; fixtures; dashboard/case history; and a later approved build or lifecycle disposition. This documentation-only review installed no update, executed no search, and created no regulatory evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At 2026-07-29T12:00:00Z configure cohort `standard` to approve build `25G86`. Add expected IDs `mac-old`, `mac-stale`, and `mac-missing`. Index `mac-old` at 11:00 with OS `26.5`, build `25F90`; `mac-stale` at 2026-07-28T11:59:59Z with approved build; and no event for missing. Expect `build_not_approved`, `inventory_stale` age 86401, and `not_observed_in_48h`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Require zero rows for exact approved build `25G86` exactly 86400 seconds old or newer; inactive/future/expired inventory; an unexpected observed device; or an exact future exception with reason, ticket, and owner. Expiry equal to dispatch does not suppress. A lexically higher but unlisted build remains unapproved, and a listed OS version with a different build remains unapproved.

dataSources: Apple MDM `DeviceInformation` query for `OSVersion` and `BuildVersion`, exported by the selected management service with exact device ID, model identifier, response/command ID, status time, tenant, collection time, API/pagination status, and collector version. Normalize to `index=endpoint_inventory`, `sourcetype=local:apple:device_information`, `device_id`, `platform`, `os_version`, `os_build`, and `model_identifier`; these are local storage/alias conventions. Policy comes from `approved_macos_builds.csv`, curated from Apple security releases, Apple update declarations/status, hardware support, testing, and organizational risk—not scraped blindly from a latest-version label.
app: Apple device management and the selected MDM vendor provide OS/build inventory. A deployment-owned collector and Splunk search app provide exact-build policy, expected inventory, exceptions, fixtures, search, dashboard, and runbook. No Universal Forwarder endpoint command or Splunkbase add-on is required.
spl:
| inputlookup expected_macos_update_policy.csv
| eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), policy_cohort=lower(trim(policy_cohort)), monitor_from_epoch=tonumber(monitor_from_epoch), monitor_until_epoch=tonumber(monitor_until_epoch), expected_row=1
| where lower(trim(monitor_enabled))="true" AND platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0 AND len(policy_cohort)>0 AND monitor_from_epoch<=now() AND monitor_until_epoch>now()
| fields device_id policy_cohort expected_row device_name serial_number owner criticality runbook
| append [ search index=endpoint_inventory sourcetype=local:apple:device_information earliest=-48h latest=now
    | eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), observed_row=1
    | where platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0
    | stats latest(_time) AS inventory_time latest(os_version) AS os_version latest(os_build) AS os_build latest(model_identifier) AS model_identifier latest(response_status) AS response_status latest(collector_time) AS collector_time by device_id ]
| stats max(expected_row) AS expected_row max(observed_row) AS observed_row values(policy_cohort) AS policy_cohort values(device_name) AS device_name values(serial_number) AS serial_number values(owner) AS owner values(criticality) AS criticality values(runbook) AS runbook max(inventory_time) AS inventory_time values(os_version) AS os_version values(os_build) AS os_build values(model_identifier) AS model_identifier values(response_status) AS response_status max(collector_time) AS collector_time by device_id
| where expected_row=1
| lookup approved_macos_builds.csv policy_cohort os_build OUTPUT build_approved policy_revision policy_source policy_valid_until_epoch
| eval inventory_age_seconds=if(isnull(inventory_time),null(),now()-inventory_time), policy_valid_until_epoch=tonumber(policy_valid_until_epoch), finding=case(isnull(observed_row),"not_observed_in_48h",inventory_age_seconds>86400,"inventory_stale",len(os_version)=0 OR len(os_build)=0,"missing_version_or_build",lower(trim(build_approved))!="true","build_not_approved",policy_valid_until_epoch<=now(),"approval_expired",true(),"healthy")
| where finding!="healthy"
| lookup macos_update_policy_exceptions.csv device_id OUTPUT exception_until_epoch exception_reason ticket exception_owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=tonumber(exception_until_epoch), exception_active=if(exception_until_epoch>now() AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(ticket)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0,1,0)
| where exception_active=0
| eval inventory_stale_seconds=86400, observation_window_hours=48, use_case_id="UC-1.3.4"
| table device_id device_name serial_number policy_cohort finding os_version os_build model_identifier inventory_time inventory_age_seconds build_approved policy_revision policy_source policy_valid_until_epoch response_status collector_time owner criticality runbook inventory_stale_seconds observation_window_hours use_case_id
| sort 0 finding policy_cohort os_build device_id
description: Runs daily and emits one row per active expected Mac when MDM OS/build inventory is missing for 48 hours, older than 24 hours, incomplete, not an exact approved `(policy_cohort,os_build)` pair, or matched to an expired approval. It preserves policy revision/source, build/model, collection evidence, lifecycle, and owner.
value: Exact build posture identifies Macs outside a reviewed update ring without treating version strings as numbers or assuming every model can run the newest release. Owners get a reproducible policy decision and evidence needed to plan updates, resolve unsupported hardware, or repair inventory collection.
implementation: Collect Apple DeviceInformation OS/build state through MDM, preserve API and device identity, and govern expected devices by tested update cohort. Maintain exact approved builds with Apple source, model support, effective/expiry dates, approver, and policy revision. Run daily, alert by device/finding, and use finite exceptions. Manage update enforcement and declarative status separately; verify successful installation with a fresh DeviceInformation response.
visualization: Lead with MDM inventory freshness/errors and policy-table health. Show unapproved, stale, absent, incomplete, and expired approval by cohort/model/owner; build distribution and age; policy revision/source. Drill down to Apple release, update declaration/status, hardware eligibility, exception, incident, and post-update build. Do not call all non-latest supported builds vulnerable or noncompliant.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; no CIM mapping is asserted for Apple OS/build inventory and local exact-build policy.

knownFalsePositives:
A row is outside the current local policy but may have an approved operational cause.

1. **Phased rollout or compatibility hold** — A ring can intentionally remain on an older build. Confirm cohort, tested application/driver issue, owner, risk acceptance, deadline, and replacement/upgrade plan; encode an approved build or exact finite exception.

2. **Unsupported hardware** — A model may not support the target release. Verify Apple's model support and asset plan; assign a distinct governed cohort rather than suppress all old hardware.

3. **Recent update awaiting next inventory** — The Mac may already have restarted into the approved build after dispatch. Confirm current MDM DeviceInformation and collect a new event; preserve the original row.

4. **MDM query/policy-table defect** — Missing page, stale collector, typo/case/whitespace, expired policy row, or wrong cohort can create findings. Check canary, response status, exact build, policy revision/signature, and lookup ACL before endpoint action.

**Suppression mechanism:** the SPL uses `lookup macos_update_policy_exceptions.csv` on exact `device_id` with future expiry, reason, ticket, and owner. Expired, wildcard, fleet-wide, collector-outage, or unsigned policy exceptions do not suppress.
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Apple DeviceInformation OS/build fields, declarative update target/status guidance and security-release records plus Splunk exact lookup/scheduled-search documentation; MDM/macOS/Splunk versions, hardware support, policy, fields, inventory, SPL, fixtures, freshness, exceptions, alerting, update response, and production behavior were specified but not executed or Apple/MDM/Splunk/endpoint/application/vulnerability/regulatory-SME signed
detailedImplementation:
## Build policy and collection

Assign Apple endpoint, MDM, application compatibility, vulnerability, asset, Splunk, and change owners. Qualify MDM/macOS/Splunk versions; this review ran none. Use MDM DeviceInformation to collect exact `OSVersion`, `BuildVersion`, model, device/command identity, status time, and API collection health. Do not compare versions as strings: for example, lexical ordering does not express Apple's release support or model applicability.

Create `expected_macos_update_policy.csv` with exact device ID, `policy_cohort`, platform, lifecycle epochs, serial, owner, criticality, and runbook. Create signed `approved_macos_builds.csv` keyed by exact `policy_cohort,os_build`, with `build_approved=true`, policy revision, Apple source, approver, effective date, expiry, tested models, and rationale. Review Apple security releases and declarative update documentation, but require compatibility/risk owners to approve each cohort. Reconcile daily and reject duplicate keys, blank builds, expired approval, unknown cohorts, and stale sources.

Collect at least daily into the local source type and monitor API pagination, response failures, canary, object count, duplicate IDs, missing OS/build/model, index delay, and collector version. `macos_update_policy_exceptions.csv` is exact, finite, and separately approved.

## Search and tests

Save `expected_macos_approved_build_posture`, schedule daily, and trigger per device/finding. Inventory starts the search, so absence is visible. Exact lookup match defines approval; no hard-coded `14.3` and no fleet count hides the device row. Exactly 86400 seconds is fresh. Route broad missing/stale findings to MDM data owners; route isolated build findings to cohort owners.

Run the specified controls plus same version/different build, same build/different cohort, blank/null/case/whitespace, policy expiry equality, 86399/86400/86401 freshness, newer duplicate, lifecycle/exception boundaries, unsupported model, re-enrollment ID, collector page loss, policy rollback, and update/restart. Compare a lab Mac's `OSVersion`/`BuildVersion` with MDM and Apple's release record. Keep draft until owners accept policy governance, versions, fixtures, alerting, and response.

## Response and limits

Triage collector and policy health first; then exact device/cohort/lifecycle; MDM inventory; model eligibility; update declaration/status/error; power, disk, network, deferral, deadline, and compatibility hold. Use Apple's declarative software-update configuration/status for enforcement and progress where supported; this inventory rule only evaluates the resulting build.

Do not automatically install, force restart, clear deferrals, change cohort, approve a build, or remove security improvements from Splunk. Use staged update change control and rollback. Close after a fresh MDM response reports an exact approved build and the affected applications pass validation. Track apps, browser versions, Background Security Improvements, vulnerability exposure, and regulatory evidence separately.
grandmaExplanation: We compare each expected Mac’s exact system build with the builds approved for its rollout group. Missing, old, or unapproved records are reviewed without assuming every Mac can run the same newest version.
